port.name: Posting
port.description: Living Code for Posting: native YAML palettes for HTTP requests, response status, syntax colors, focus and layered UI surfaces.

guide.installation:
```sh
flavor=night # night, frost, paper, or signal
theme_dir="$(posting locate themes | tail -n 1)"
curl -fsSL --create-dirs -o "$theme_dir/living-code-$flavor.yaml" "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/living-code-theme/posting/main/themes/living-code-$flavor.yaml"
POSTING_THEME="living-code-$flavor" posting
```

`posting locate themes` prints a heading followed by the application’s actual theme directory; `tail -n 1` selects only that path. The download therefore works with custom and platform-specific data locations. Restart an already running Posting instance after adding a new file. No existing config or collection is replaced.
guide.configuration: To keep a flavor permanently, set `theme: living-code-night` in Posting’s existing config. You can preview themes through **Ctrl+P → Theme…**. Each YAML file declares its name, light/dark appearance and all supported base palette colors. Posting derives HTTP method and syntax colors from those palette fields; no ignored legacy syntax blocks are shipped.
guide.compatibility:
Targets Posting 2.11+’s native palette API; the same base fields are also understood by Posting 2, but version-specific rendering is not claimed. Paper explicitly sets `dark: false`. `load_user_themes` must be enabled, and `theme_directory` may override the default location. Tests parse YAML and verify the documented supported field set.

Previews are captured programmatically from the actual application in an isolated profile. See [`capture/app.py`](capture/app.py) for the app-owned recipe and [`images/capture.json`](images/capture.json) for runtime, palette and image provenance. No mock interface is drawn.
